co_5_cartoon_wall.blurb: Cartoon Wall is a short stretch of the east end of Dines Cliff, up in Staunton State Park in the South Platte country. Fourteen lines mix bolted sport routes with gear leads and a handful of top-rope setups, so it suits a party with a bit of everything. Most of the climbing is 5.10 and 5.11, with a few 5.9s and a lone 5.8 to warm up on. The granite is reported to be good, and trees throw some shade over the base while the wall still picks up sun. Routes carry the names of TV cartoon characters. The short side trail from the main cliff path ends at the base.

co_acid_rock.blurb: Acid Rock is the middle tower in the group that runs from Helen's Dome across to the summit face of Sheep Rock, in the South Platte area near Goose Creek. It rises roughly 500 to 600 feet, though the cleanest climbing is packed into the lower 200 to 400 feet. Granite slabs dominate, with a few worthwhile cracks, and many lines run two to four pitches. Of the 14 routes here, nine are trad and five are sport, running from 5.7 up to the low 5.11 range with most between 5.9 and 5.10. Some routes are run out, so expect serious slab leads and bring a rack for the crack lines.

co_alpha_beta_gamma_delta_block.blurb: This is the first group of rocks you meet in the V-Naughts, a small sandstone bouldering zone inside Ute Valley Park in Colorado Springs. Fourteen problems sit here, labelled with Greek letters, and nearly all are V0 with only two nudging up to V1. That makes it a relaxed spot for beginners, families and anyone wanting an easy warm-up circuit rather than a destination session. The stone is of mixed quality, so test holds and pull down instead of out. A slot behind the Delta boulder lets you walk off the top. Expect an hour or less of fun.

co_lower_swallow_crag.blurb: Lower Swallow Crag is a big, tall granite cliff in the Swallow Crags group near Red Feather Lakes, northwest of Fort Collins. It is the third cliff you meet on the cairned climber's trail, beginning just left of Little Swallow Crag, and it shows south and west faces. Climbs are long with generally sound rock and are regarded as some of the best around Red Feather. Of the 14 listed, ten are trad, three sport and one is a boulder problem, and the grades lean hard: mostly 5.11 and 5.12, with one 5.13 line. This is a place for experienced leaders rather than beginners.

co_lower_ice_caves.blurb: Lower Ice Caves is a sport climbing section within Rifle Mountain Park, in the limestone canyon outside Rifle, Colorado. A cave forms here where a trail passes beneath a seeping wall, and the routes sit around it. All 14 lines are bolted. Four are 5.10, nine are 5.11 and a single route reaches 5.12, so it is a good fit for climbers in the low-to-mid 5.11 range who want established lines rather than hard projects. Several of the routes are older moderate classics, with one excellent newer extension of an older line.
